The journal print was not read, so the number Theorem 31 in print rests on a search snippet of the Imperial copy. The structure of the proof (Theorem 41, Props 45-47) was read; the proof was not re-derived. *Scope.* Z = K_P2 x C^2 is the smooth toric variety with N = Z^5, rays b_0 = (1,0,1,0,0), b_1 = (0,1,1,0,0), b_2 = (-1,-1,1,0,0), b_3 = (0,0,1,0,0), b_4 = (0,0,0,1,0), b_5 = (0,0,0,0,1), and maximal cones spanned by b_3, b_4, b_5 and two of b_0, b_1, b_2. These cones are unimodular, so Box = {0}, and L = Z(1,1,1,-3,0,0). Z is semi-projective in the sense of CCIT15 s.3.1: it has three fixed points, and Z -> Spec H^0(O_Z) = C^3/mu_3 x C^2 is projective, with -D_3 = 3H relatively ample. In fan terms the support Cone(b_0,b_1,b_2) x R_{>=0}^2 is convex and full-dimensional, and the piecewise linear function with value -1 at b_3 and 0 at the other rays is the maximum of its linear pieces, strictly. NE(Z) is generated by the line. *Torus.* CCIT15's torus is N x C^* = (C^*)^6/C^*. BS's T_max (weights (alpha_0,alpha_1,alpha_2,0,-eps1,-eps2) on C^6, BS line 2349) maps onto it with kernel mu_3. The character lattices differ by index 3, so S_T = C(alpha_0,alpha_1,alpha_2,eps1,eps2) = Q_{T_max}, and the localisation formulas agree. *Dictionary.* For the T_max action the toric divisor classes are u_i = H + alpha_i (i = 0,1,2), u_3 = -3H, u_4 = -eps1, u_5 = -eps2, with H = c_1 of O(1) with its BS lift, H|P_i = -alpha_i. So H = -u_3/3, alpha_i = u_i - H, eps_j = -u_{3+j}. Then u_j|P_i are BS's tangent weights w^{(j)}_i (BS line 2383), and the relation u_0 u_1 u_2 = 0 is BS's prod(H + alpha_i) = 0. *Substitution.* Take S empty and all t_i = 0 in (19). Then lambda = d(1,1,1,-3,0,0), d >= 0, and the factors are 1/prod_{m=1}^d (H+alpha_i+mz) for i = 0,1,2, prod_{m=0}^{3d-1}(-3H-mz) for i = 3, and 1 for i = 4,5. So I_CCIT(Q,z) = z Sum_d Q^d I_d(z), where z y^{H/z} Sum_d y^d I_d(z) is eq:Ifun. *Mirror map.* Each summand with d >= 1 is -3H times a function homogeneous of degree -1 in (H,alpha,z), with expansion at z = infinity beginning 3H(-1)^d (3d-1)!/(d!)^3 z^{-1}. Reducing H^3 by the relation keeps the power of z. Hence I_CCIT(Q,-z) = -z + g(Q)H + O(1/z), with g(Q) = 3 Sum_{d>=1} (3d-1)!/(d!)^3 (-Q)^d independent of alpha and g(0) = 0; g = I_0^{[1]} - log y in the notation of eq:Ian. Theorem 31 says this is a point (4). The H_+ part of (4) is -z + t(z), so t(z) = g(Q)H, and by Remark 3 I_CCIT(Q,z) = J(g(Q)H,z). *Divisor equation.* J(tau H,z) = z e^{tau H/z}(1 + Sum_d (Q e^{tau})^d <<phi_a/(z(z-psi))>>_{0,1,d} phi^a), including the d = 0 classical terms z e^{tau H/z}. (51)), which is BS's Notation at line 1233 for this Z and T. A1.1 and A1.2 identify this with the twisted integral on Mbar_{0,n}(P2,d) in genus 0. For d = 0, Mbar_{0,n}(Z,0) = Mbar_{0,n} x Z, and both sides are Sum_i prod a_j|P_i /W_i^0 times a psi integral on Mbar_{0,n}; the pairing is BS's eta. On genus-0 trees R pi_* f^* O_w = O_w, so the C^2 factor multiplies each invariant by 1/(eps1 eps2) and eta^{ab} by eps1 eps2, and J is unchanged. *Inputs of CCIT15's proof.* Brown's recursive characterisation of the cone in the form of Theorem 41; Liu's localisation formula; the Coates-Givental/CCIT hypergeometric modification with Tseng's quantum Riemann-Roch at the fixed points (here BG_sigma is a point, so that theory is on Mbar_{0,n}); and Theorem 2, whose TRR is the genus-0 psi-class relation. This gives the genus-0 topological recursion relation (TRR) of the theory of Z, namely <<c, a, psi^{k+1} b>> = Sum_{e,f} <<psi^k b, e>> eta^{ef} <<f, c, a>>, with only stable splittings on the right. Restrict to t_0 = t_2 = 0, t_1 = log Q, where d_1 = theta_Q. WDVV is not used; commutativity of the operators c* follows by comparing z d_c z d_e with z d_e z d_c, since S(a) = a + O(1/z) is invertible. Same form of (6) and of the fundamental solution: Pandharipande s.1.2 (6), s.1.3 Prop 2.
